title: Cardiometabolic benefits of parathyroidectomy in dialysis patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism: preliminary insights from CT radiomics and body composition analysis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Cardiometabolic benefits of parathyroidectomy in dialysis patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism: preliminary insights from CT radiomics and body composition analysis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p5】In this study, we aimed to investigate post-PTX EAT remodeling, vascular calcification, and body composition changes in patients with SHPT undergoing dialysis and to ascertain their implications for cardiometabolic health.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT), which is characterized by disturbances in mineral metabolism, is a common and serious complication in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) that significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality [1,2]. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is an endocrine peptide, and the parathyroid-related proteins are expressed in various tissues and exert diverse biological effects [3–6]. In SHPT, elevated PTH levels can induce increased bone resorption, hypercalcemia, protein-energy wasting, malnutrition, and cachexia [4–6]. SHPT potentially activates cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent protein kinase A, which subsequently activates thermogenic genes to increase resting energy expenditure to induce adipose tissue browning and loss of fat and muscle [3,7–9]. Thus, SHPT may be associated with higher resting energy expenditure and could contribute to morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing dialysis. [10]. Furthermore, as hyperparathyroidism treatments may alter body composition, which modifies morbidity and mortality risks, the changes in higher fat composition that were associated with a higher body mass index (BMI) in patients with ESRD on dialysis were associated with improved survival [11].

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT), which is characterized by disturbances in mineral metabolism, is a common and serious complication in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) that significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality [1,2]. 【Introduction · S0001-p2】Current medical management of SHPT includes administration of vitamin D analogs, calcimimetics, and phosphate binders, which are associated with various degrees of vascular calcification [12]. Parathyroidectomy (PTX), which is typically reserved for patients with severe SHPT, can rapidly reduce the circulating PTH levels. Moreover, in patients with ESRD and severe hyperparathyroidism, PTX decreases cardiovascular mortality risk [13,14]. However, whether PTX in patients with SHPT can induce cardiometabolic changes that improve protein-energy wasting remains unclear.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Cardiometabolic benefits of parathyroidectomy in dialysis patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism: preliminary insights from CT radiomics and body composition analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · S0003-p1】We enrolled 51 patients with severe hyperparathyroidism. Of these, 30 initially chose PTX with follow-up CT; however, only 21 underwent surgery within the study period and completed CT and DXA body composition assessments. Nineteen patients opted for conservative medical management, and subsequently, 16 of them completed follow-up CT and DXA within the study period. Eight patients underwent preoperative CT and DXA assessments within one month prior to PTX, while 13 patients completed these evaluations 1–2 months before surgery. Postoperative CT and DXA assessments were performed at approximately six months. Control subjects underwent baseline and follow-up testing at comparable six-month intervals (Figure 2).

【Results · S0003-p2】Within the PTX group, one patient underwent subtotal PTX, one underwent total PTX due to local recurrence after prior surgery, and the remaining 19 underwent total PTX with auto-implantation. Baseline demographic, anthropometric, and biochemical parameters are summarized in Table 1. There were no significant between-group differences in age, sex, BMI, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia. The PTX dialysis group exhibited a higher, though non-significant, degree of coronary artery calcification (CAC) compared with the non-PTX group. Both groups demonstrated a similar EAT radiomic phenotype, whereas the PTX group had significantly higher PTH levels than the non-PTX group (p < 0.01).

sections.title: 图表阅读

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Native ECG-gated non-contrast computed tomography (CT). Green arrow indicates ParaAT: paracardiac adipose tissue; white arrowhead indicates epicardial adipose tissue (EAT). The EAT appears more yellow (higher attenuation) than ParaAT, suggesting increased inflammatory activity, as demonstrated by the color-coded adipose tissue highlights.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Study flowchart. Flow diagram illustrating patient enrollment, group allocation, and follow-up. Patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) undergoing dialysis were assigned to either the parathyroidectomy group or the non-parathyroidectomy control group.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Epicardial Adipose Tissue Volume (EATV) vs. Epicardial Adipose Tissue Attenuation (EATAT); serum PTH levels before PTX vs. EATAT. (A) Scatter plot showing the negative correlation between EATV and EATAT mean (r = −0.566, p < 0.001). (B) Serum parathyroid hormone levels in Patients with SHPT undergoing dialysis were assigned to either the parathyroidectomy group or the non-parathyroidectomy control group vs. EATAT mean (r = 0.368, p = 0.025). (C) Scatter plot showing the negative correlation between changes in EATV and EATAT mean (r = −0.444, p = 0.006). (D) Distribution of EATV and EATAT mean changes in the parathyroidectomy group vs. the non-parathyroidectomy group. Parathyroidectomy was associated with increased EATV and decreased attenuation, suggesting a shift toward less inflamed, lipid-rich adipose tissue.
